plan.english: In the night Of-Good-Fame, the brave warrior, came to the fields of the enemy. There the cows were grazing. He seized them and drove them home. A shepherd saw him and ran to the chief. Then the chief and his sons followed their tracks. At the ford they found him. The chief threw his spear. Of-Good-Fame pierced the chief with his spear, and he fell. They became afraid of him and fled. Then Of-Good-Fame drove them to his own village. His fame was great.

clauses.english: In the night Of-Good-Fame, the brave warrior, came to the fields of the enemy.
There the cows were grazing.
He seized them and drove them home.
A shepherd saw him and ran to the chief.
Then the chief and his sons followed their tracks.
At the ford they found him.
The chief threw his spear.
Of-Good-Fame pierced the chief with his spear, and he fell.
They became afraid of him and fled.
Then Of-Good-Fame drove them to his own village.
His fame was great.

plan.english: The chief prepared a great feast in his house. Many warriors came to the feast. He seated them near the fire and filled their cups with mead. They ate meat and drank the sweet mead. Then he stood up and spoke. Warriors, hear my words! To the bravest man I give a horse and a cup of gold. Then the warrior Man-Minded answered. I slew the serpent at the river. They praised him, and the chief gave him the prize. His fame is imperishable.

clauses.english: The chief prepared a great feast in his house.
Many warriors came to the feast.
He seated them near the fire and filled their cups with mead.
They ate meat and drank the sweet mead.
Then he stood up and spoke.
Warriors, hear my words!
To the bravest man I give a horse and a cup of gold.
Then the warrior Man-Minded answered.
I slew the serpent at the river.
They praised him, and the chief gave him the prize.
His fame is imperishable.

plan.english: If anyone steals a calf, he pays a cow. If anyone steals a bull, he pays a hundred sheep. If anyone steals a goat, let him give back two goats. If the master of the house kills a thief in the night, he does not pay a blood-price. If he kills him by day, he pays the blood-price to his kin. Whoever hides a thief in his house, he too is a thief.

clauses.english: If anyone steals a calf, he pays a cow.
If anyone steals a bull, he pays a hundred sheep.
If anyone steals a goat, let him give back two goats.
If the master of the house kills a thief in the night, he does not pay a blood-price.
If he kills him by day, he pays the blood-price to his kin.
Whoever hides a thief in his house, he too is a thief.

title: The Storm God and the Serpent

plan.english: The serpent stole the cows of the gods. He hid them in the stone. The gods searched for them and did not find them. Then Perkunos came. He slew the serpent with his spear. He split the stone, and the herd came out. Then they gave a beautiful bull to Perkunos. Whoever steals cattle, Perkunos strikes him.

clauses.english: The serpent stole the cows of the gods.
He hid them in the stone.
The gods searched for them and did not find them.
Then Perkunos came.
He slew the serpent with his spear.
He split the stone, and the herd came out.
Then they gave a beautiful bull to Perkunos.
Whoever steals cattle, Perkunos strikes him.

plan.english: Two warriors were fighting at the ford. The one was Of-Goodly-Fame, the son of a king. The other was a stranger, Fame-from-the-Gods. Of-Goodly-Fame threw his spear, and it struck the shield. Then Fame-from-the-Gods threw his spear. He wounded him. Of-Goodly-Fame fell into the water. Then Fame-from-the-Gods spoke to him. Of-Goodly-Fame, do not be afraid of me. I will not kill you. Then he took him from the water and carried him to his father.

Then Fame-from-the-Gods threw his spear.
He wounded him.
Of-Goodly-Fame fell into the water.
Then Fame-from-the-Gods spoke to him.
Of-Goodly-Fame, do not be afraid of me.
I will not kill you.
Then he took him from the water and carried him to his father.

plan.english: A young warrior vowed to the chief. I will guard your cattle. The chief gave him a blade. In the night he led them to the enemy, who gave him gold. He broke his word. At dawn the chief went into the cow-stall and did not find them. Dyeus saw the lie. Dyeus struck the one who had broken his word, and he died. Do not deceive your lord!

I will guard your cattle.
The chief gave him a blade.
In the night he led them to the enemy, who gave him gold.
He broke his word.
At dawn the chief went into the cow-stall and did not find them.
Dyeus saw the lie.
Dyeus struck the one who had broken his word, and he died.
Do not deceive your lord!

plan.english: If a guest comes to a house, the host gives him meat and mead. If he steals anything from the host, let the host drive him out. When he goes away, the host gives him a gift, and he praises the host. A guest is holy. Whoever kills a guest, let him pay the blood-price twice.

clauses.english: If a guest comes to a house, the host gives him meat and mead.
If he steals anything from the host, let the host drive him out.
When he goes away, the host gives him a gift, and he praises the host.
A guest is holy.
Whoever kills a guest, let him pay the blood-price twice.

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses struck the brother of Of-Divine-Race, and he died. Of-Divine-Race wept. Then he took his spear and went to Of-Good-Horses. Of-Good-Horses came out and spoke. Do not kill me! I will pay you the blood-price, a hundred cows. Of-Divine-Race was angry. Then the old men of the village spoke. Take the blood-price and let him live. Of-Divine-Race heeded the old men. He took them, and Of-Good-Horses lived.

Do not kill me!
I will pay you the blood-price, a hundred cows.

Take the blood-price and let him live.
Of-Divine-Race heeded the old men.
He took them, and Of-Good-Horses lived.

plan.english: It was getting dark. An old man arrived at the house of a villager. The villager's wife questioned him. Where are you going? I am a mortal from another land. Her husband seated him near the fire. The wife gave him milk and meat. He ate and drank and fell asleep. In the morning he stood up and spoke to the villager. May the gods give you good things! I am a god. Then he went away, and the villager's herd grew large.

I am a mortal from another land.

He ate and drank and fell asleep.

May the gods give you good things!
I am a god.

plan.english: Enemies drove away the cattle of the chief. Then he spoke to his three sons. Take your spears and follow them! They yoked the horses and drove through the night. At dawn they caught sight of the hostile men at the river. They became afraid and left the herd. The sons took it and drove it to the village. The chief rejoiced and gave them gold. Swift horses and brave sons are the wealth of a chief.

Take your spears and follow them!

The sons took it and drove it to the village.
The chief rejoiced and gave them gold.
Swift horses and brave sons are the wealth of a chief.

plan.english: The cows of Dawn were in a stone. An evil serpent guarded them. Mortals trembled in fear of the night. Then the young god led his swift horses to the stone. He slew the serpent and split the stone. They came forth, and Dawn grew bright. In the morning the cows of Dawn come out of the stone. Mortals praise him.

An evil serpent guarded them.

In the morning the cows of Dawn come out of the stone.
Mortals praise him.

plan.english: If anyone slays a man, he gives the blood-price to the kin of the dead man. The blood-price of a free man is a hundred cows. The blood-price of a servant is ten sheep. If the killer does not pay, the kin of the dead man take revenge on him. If anyone wounds a man, he pays a sheep. Whoever kills his host at a feast, Dyeus hates him.

clauses.english: If anyone slays a man, he gives the blood-price to the kin of the dead man.

The blood-price of a servant is ten sheep.
If the killer does not pay, the kin of the dead man take revenge on him.
If anyone wounds a man, he pays a sheep.
Whoever kills his host at a feast, Dyeus hates him.

plan.english: The king of the people was sitting in his great house. A singer came to him. He praised the king's father, who had slain the serpent. The lord was glad. He gave him ten oxen, a cup of gold and a hundred sheep. King, you are a giver of good things! May your fame be imperishable!

clauses.english: The king of the people was sitting in his great house.
A singer came to him.
He praised the king's father, who had slain the serpent.
The lord was glad.
He gave him ten oxen, a cup of gold and a hundred sheep.
King, you are a giver of good things!
May your fame be imperishable!

plan.english: In the night a thief came to a cow-stall. He was looking for a fat bull. The dog was awake. The dog watched him and seized his leg. He howled and fled. In the morning the shepherd found his spear in the cow-stall. Then he gave the dog meat. A good dog is dearer than gold.

clauses.english: In the night a thief came to a cow-stall.

The dog was awake.
The dog watched him and seized his leg.
He howled and fled.
In the morning the shepherd found his spear in the cow-stall.
Then he gave the dog meat.
A good dog is dearer than gold.

plan.english: Of-Goodly-Fame went to war with his lord. He vowed to his wife. I will return home in the summer. He overpowered many hostile men. His wife was weaving at her loom. In the summer he returned home unharmed. His wife rejoiced, because he had not broken his word.

clauses.english: Of-Goodly-Fame went to war with his lord.
He vowed to his wife.
I will return home in the summer.
He overpowered many hostile men.
His wife was weaving at her loom.
In the summer he returned home unharmed.
His wife rejoiced, because he had not broken his word.

plan.english: A great serpent lay around the waters. The rivers were dry. The herds were thirsty, and mortals wept. Then Perkunos took his spear. He came to the serpent and struck it. He slew the serpent and freed the waters. The rivers became full. The herd drank, and mortals praised Perkunos. May he protect our cattle!

clauses.english: A great serpent lay around the waters.
The rivers were dry.
The herds were thirsty, and mortals wept.
Then Perkunos took his spear.
He came to the serpent and struck it.
He slew the serpent and freed the waters.
The rivers became full.
The herd drank, and mortals praised Perkunos.
May he protect our cattle!

plan.english: If anyone swears a lie, the assembly punishes him. If anyone breaks a pledge to the chief, he pays him ten oxen. Whoever swears an oath in the assembly, let him not break it. Whoever breaks an oath, he is not of good fame. Let no one swear against his own father.

clauses.english: If anyone swears a lie, the assembly punishes him.
If anyone breaks a pledge to the chief, he pays him ten oxen.
Whoever swears an oath in the assembly, let him not break it.
Whoever breaks an oath, he is not of good fame.
Let no one swear against his own father.

title: The Old King at the Ford

plan.english: Of-Good-Horses was young and bold. He drove away the horses of an old king. The lord followed him to the ford. There he spoke. Young man, stand and fight with me! The two fought with spears in the water. The lord struck his shield, and the shield split. Then the young man threw down his spear. I will give them back to you. I vow to you. I will not steal from you again. The lord took them and let him go. Of-Good-Horses did not break his word.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Horses was young and bold.
He drove away the horses of an old king.
The lord followed him to the ford.
There he spoke.
Young man, stand and fight with me!
The two fought with spears in the water.
The lord struck his shield, and the shield split.
Then the young man threw down his spear.
I will give them back to you.
I vow to you.
I will not steal from you again.
The lord took them and let him go.
Of-Good-Horses did not break his word.

plan.english: Two brothers lived in a village. The one had many cows, and the other had few. In the evening he stole a bull from his brother. He hid it in his own cow-stall. In the morning the master of the bull searched for it. He followed its tracks to the cow-stall of the other. Why did you steal my bull? The other answered. My children are hungry. Then he gave him the bull and ten sheep. A brother does not take revenge on a brother.

clauses.english: Two brothers lived in a village.
The one had many cows, and the other had few.
In the evening he stole a bull from his brother.
He hid it in his own cow-stall.
In the morning the master of the bull searched for it.
He followed its tracks to the cow-stall of the other.
Why did you steal my bull?
The other answered.
My children are hungry.
Then he gave him the bull and ten sheep.
A brother does not take revenge on a brother.

plan.english: In the summer the young warriors went against the hostile men. Their hearts were bold. For nine nights they marched. They crossed three mountains. Then they caught sight of herds in a field. Then the wise one spoke. Let us drive away this herd! They led the herd away, and its masters did not see them. In the village the women praised them. Their fame became great.

clauses.english: In the summer the young warriors went against the hostile men.
Their hearts were bold.
For nine nights they marched.
They crossed three mountains.
Then they caught sight of herds in a field.
Then the wise one spoke.
Let us drive away this herd!
They led the herd away, and its masters did not see them.
In the village the women praised them.
Their fame became great.

plan.english: If a chief prepares a feast, he gives gifts to his men. Whoever takes a gift, he owes a gift. If anyone is sitting at the feast, let no one strike him. Let the bravest warrior eat the best meat. If two men grow angry at the feast, the elders decide.

clauses.english: If a chief prepares a feast, he gives gifts to his men.
Whoever takes a gift, he owes a gift.
If anyone is sitting at the feast, let no one strike him.
Let the bravest warrior eat the best meat.
If two men grow angry at the feast, the elders decide.

title: The Chief Who Did Not Give

plan.english: There was an old chief who did not give gifts. His warriors were hungry and thirsty. In the night they left him. They went to another lord, who gave them meat and gold. Then hostile men came to the village of the chief. They drove off his herds, and no one protected him. He sat down and wept. He who gives is dear to his men.

clauses.english: There was an old chief who did not give gifts.
His warriors were hungry and thirsty.
In the night they left him.
They went to another lord, who gave them meat and gold.
Then hostile men came to the village of the chief.
They drove off his herds, and no one protected him.
He sat down and wept.
He who gives is dear to his men.

plan.english: The enemies were standing at the ford. Their spears were many. Then Kindly, the chief, spoke to his men. Warriors, do not be afraid of them! Our fathers fought at this crossing. Let us cross the river and strike them! Whoever falls, his fame will be imperishable. They took shields and spears. They crossed the water and overpowered them.

clauses.english: The enemies were standing at the ford.
Their spears were many.
Then Kindly, the chief, spoke to his men.
Warriors, do not be afraid of them!
Our fathers fought at this crossing.
Let us cross the river and strike them!
Whoever falls, his fame will be imperishable.
They took shields and spears.
They crossed the water and overpowered them.

plan.english: Mortals had no cattle. They were hungry. Then Father Dyeus caught sight of them. He took cows from his own herd and gave them to the people. Guard them and milk them! Give the best one to the gods! People drink milk.

clauses.english: Mortals had no cattle.
They were hungry.
Then Father Dyeus caught sight of them.
He took cows from his own herd and gave them to the people.
Guard them and milk them!
Give the best one to the gods!
People drink milk.

plan.english: If a stranger enters the village, let the villagers ask his name. If he says his name, he is a guest. If he does not say his name, he is an enemy. Whoever strikes a guest, he gives ten goats to the chief. Whoever slays him, let his own kin throw him out.

clauses.english: If a stranger enters the village, let the villagers ask his name.
If he says his name, he is a guest.
If he does not say his name, he is an enemy.
Whoever strikes a guest, he gives ten goats to the chief.
Whoever slays him, let his own kin throw him out.

plan.english: An evil man killed the husband of a woman. The woman went to the king with her son. King, my husband is dead. Who will pay the blood-price for him? He answered. The killer will pay you a hundred cows. The killer fled. Then her child grew up and became a strong warrior. He found the killer and pierced him. He took vengeance for his father.

The woman went to the king with her son.
King, my husband is dead.
Who will pay the blood-price for him?
He answered.
The killer will pay you a hundred cows.
The killer fled.
Then her child grew up and became a strong warrior.
He found the killer and pierced him.
He took vengeance for his father.

plan.english: Of-Good-Fame died at the ford. His brother carried the dead man home. The women and his mother wept. The men piled up wood and burned the dead man. They put his spear and shield in the fire. Then his brother spoke. Brother, your fame will not be lost. I will take the blood-price from your killer. His name is famous among the warriors.

clauses.english: Of-Good-Fame died at the ford.
His brother carried the dead man home.
The women and his mother wept.
The men piled up wood and burned the dead man.
They put his spear and shield in the fire.
Then his brother spoke.
Brother, your fame will not be lost.
I will take the blood-price from your killer.
His name is famous among the warriors.

plan.english: A wolf seized a calf from the herd. The shepherd caught sight of it and vowed. I will kill this wolf. He followed its tracks for three days. Then he found it in a field. It was eating the calf. The shepherd threw his spear and pierced it. The wolf died. He took its skin and returned home. His wife praised him.

clauses.english: A wolf seized a calf from the herd.
The shepherd caught sight of it and vowed.
I will kill this wolf.
He followed its tracks for three days.
Then he found it in a field.
It was eating the calf.
The shepherd threw his spear and pierced it.
The wolf died.
He took its skin and returned home.
His wife praised him.

plan.english: Enemies seized the son of the chief in battle. They led him away, a captive. Then the chief went to their village with gifts. Give back my son! I will give you a ransom, ten horses. Their lord answered. That ransom is small. Give us also a hundred cows! Then he gave them the ransom, and the captive returned home with him.

clauses.english: Enemies seized the son of the chief in battle.
They led him away, a captive.
Then the chief went to their village with gifts.
Give back my son!
I will give you a ransom, ten horses.
Their lord answered.
That ransom is small.
Give us also a hundred cows!
Then he gave them the ransom, and the captive returned home with him.

plan.english: If a wolf seizes a calf and the shepherd shows its hide to the master, he does not pay. If he does not show the hide, he pays a calf. If a bull goes into the field of another, its master pays a sheep to the master of the field. If thieves come in the night and the shepherd strikes them, the master gives him a gift.

clauses.english: If a wolf seizes a calf and the shepherd shows its hide to the master, he does not pay.
If he does not show the hide, he pays a calf.
If a bull goes into the field of another, its master pays a sheep to the master of the field.
If thieves come in the night and the shepherd strikes them, the master gives him a gift.

plan.english: The gods were fighting with the serpent. The serpent was great and strong. Then they went to the river and swore an oath. We will not flee from the serpent. Whoever runs away, let the river take him. They did not flee. They fought for three days. Then Perkunos struck the serpent's head with his spear, and the serpent died. The gods swear oaths at the river.

clauses.english: The gods were fighting with the serpent.
The serpent was great and strong.
Then they went to the river and swore an oath.
We will not flee from the serpent.
Whoever runs away, let the river take him.
They did not flee.
They fought for three days.
Then Perkunos struck the serpent's head with his spear, and the serpent died.
The gods swear oaths at the river.

plan.english: A young man questioned an old man. Old man, how many cows is a man worth? He answered. A man is worth a hundred cows. How many is a servant worth? Ten cows. To whom does the killer give them? To the kin of the dead man. If the killer does not give them, the kin take vengeance on him. The young man was silent.

clauses.english: A young man questioned an old man.
Old man, how many cows is a man worth?
He answered.
A man is worth a hundred cows.
How many is a servant worth?
Ten cows.
To whom does the killer give them?
To the kin of the dead man.
If the killer does not give them, the kin take vengeance on him.
The young man was silent.

plan.english: At the feast of the lord the warriors drank mead. Then Fame-from-the-Gods stood up and made a vow. I will bring back the cattle that the hostile men stole. The lord rejoiced and gave him a spear. In the morning the hero marched to their land. He overpowered them and led the herd to the lord. He carried out his vow. The lord gave him his daughter. His name became famous.

clauses.english: At the feast of the lord the warriors drank mead.

I will bring back the cattle that the hostile men stole.

plan.english: If a thief steals a horse and the master seizes him, let the master bind him and lead him to the assembly. The assembly decides his penalty. If he gives it back, he gives three oxen. If it dies, he pays its price in gold. If he has nothing, let him work for the master for a year.

clauses.english: If a thief steals a horse and the master seizes him, let the master bind him and lead him to the assembly.
The assembly decides his penalty.
If he gives it back, he gives three oxen.
If it dies, he pays its price in gold.
If he has nothing, let him work for the master for a year.

plan.english: In the winter an enemy came to the house of Kindly. He was cold and hungry. Kindly recognized him. This man had slain his father. Now he was a guest. Kindly seated him near the fire and gave him meat. He ate and lay down. In the morning Kindly spoke to him. Go away! At the ford I will look for you with my spear. He returned home unharmed.

clauses.english: In the winter an enemy came to the house of Kindly.
He was cold and hungry.
Kindly recognized him.
This man had slain his father.

He ate and lay down.

Go away!

plan.english: The warriors returned home with much plunder. They brought cattle and silver. The chief sat down on his seat and divided the plunder. He gave swift horses to the bravest warriors. He gave the silver to the singer. He led the herd into his own cow-stall. A young man was angry. Why did you give me nothing? The chief spoke to him. You fled from the battle. He who flees receives nothing.

The chief sat down on his seat and divided the plunder.

He who flees receives nothing.

plan.english: The young men of the people were slow. Hostile men came and drove away their cattle. Then the young men prayed to Dyeus. Father Dyeus, give us might! Dyeus heard them. He gave them the hearts of wolves. Then they became swift and bold. In the night they went out and overpowered them. They led their herds back.

clauses.english: The young men of the people were slow.

plan.english: If two men are fighting over a cow, let them go to the assembly. There let the two swear an oath. Dyeus knows the truth. Whoever swears the truth, let the assembly give it to him. If one does not come to the assembly, let the assembly give it to the other. Let no one swear an oath in the night.

clauses.english: If two men are fighting over a cow, let them go to the assembly.

Dyeus knows the truth.

plan.english: Ill-Minded was a thief. He came to a ford. There he saw a shepherd guarding sheep. Then he spoke to him. Friend, I have seen a wolf in the field! The shepherd ran to the field. Ill-Minded drove them away. There was no wolf. He came back and did not find them. He followed the tracks and seized him. He led him to the chief, and the thief paid ten sheep. He who deceives does not escape.

clauses.english: Ill-Minded was a thief.

There he saw a shepherd guarding sheep.
Then he spoke to him.
Friend, I have seen a wolf in the field!

Imperishable fame is dearer than a long life. They fought the whole day. Man-Minded overpowered many enemies with his spear. In the evening a spear pierced his heart. He fell into the water and died. No one crossed the water. The fame of Man-Minded is imperishable.
